claims: On April 6, 2026, the NASA Artemis II mission officially broke the 56-year-old record for the farthest distance humans have ever traveled from Earth.
The NASA Artemis II mission surpassed the 400,171 km (248,655 miles) set by Apollo 13 in 1970.
Apollo 13 set the record at 400,171 km (248,655 miles) in April 1970.
The Orion capsule reached a maximum distance of approximately 252,752 miles (406,773 km) during its lunar flyby.
Artemis II reached a maximum distance of 252,752 miles (406,773 km) in April 2026.
During the flyby, the crew came within 4,067 miles of the moon.
During the flyby, the crew traveled at approximately 3,139 mph.
The Artemis II mission crew consisted of Reid Wiseman, Jeremy Hansen, Christina Koch, and Victor Glover.
The Artemis II mission crew achieved the milestone on their 10-day, figure-eight journey around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission crew documented the far side of the Moon.
The Artemis II mission crew successfully returned to a Pacific splashdown.
